**Tafsir of Surah Sabbih (Al-A'la)**

It is Meccan.

The evidence for this is what al-Bukhari narrated: "'Abdan narrated to us: my father informed me, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The first of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) to come to us were Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum, and they began teaching us the Qur'an. Then 'Ammar, Bilal and Sa'd came. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came with twenty men. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came, and I have never seen the people of Madinah rejoice at anything as they rejoiced at that. I saw the young women and the boys saying: 'This is the Messenger of Allah, who has come.' He had not arrived until I had recited: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ and similar surahs." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4941.]

Imam Ahmad said: "Waki' narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, from his father, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved this surah: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Al-Musnad (1/961). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/136): "In its chain is Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

It is established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾, and ﴿By the night when it covers﴾?" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 705; Sahih Muslim, no. 465.]

Imam Ahmad said: "Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from Habib ibn Salim, from his father, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited in the two 'Eids: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾ And if the 'Eid coincided with Friday, he recited both of them." [Al-Musnad (4/271).]

This is how the chain of this hadith occurs in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad. Muslim in his Sahih, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, Jarir and Shu'bah, all three from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from Habib ibn Salim, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, with the same wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 878; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1122; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 533; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/112).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Likewise it was narrated by al-Thawri and Mis'ar, from Ibrahim (he said: and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated it from Ibrahim), from his father, from Habib ibn Salim, from his father, from al-Nu'man. And no narration from Habib from his father is known."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from Habib ibn Salim, from al-Nu'man, with it. [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1281.] It was narrated by the group (of compilers) as well, and Allah knows best.

The wording of Muslim and the authors of the Sunan is: "He used to recite on the two 'Eids and on Friday ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?﴾. Sometimes both coincided on one day, and he recited them both."

Imam Ahmad, in his Musnad, also narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, and 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the witr prayer ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ and ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾. [The hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b is in al-Musnad (5/123); the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in al-Musnad (1/299); the hadith of Ibn Abza in al-Musnad (3/406); the hadith of 'A'ishah in al-Musnad (6/227).]

Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e., the content of this speech, ﴿is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾.

This is a good and strong choice. It has also been related from Qatadah and Ibn Zayd something similar. And Allah knows best.

End of the tafsir of Surah "Sabbih", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, he succeeds who purifies himself﴾, meaning: he cleanses his soul of vile character and follows what Allah sent down upon His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. ﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾, meaning: he establishes the prayer at its appointed times, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, obeying the command of Allah, and complying with the law of Allah. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

Ibad ibn Ahmad al-Azrami narrated to us, my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from his father, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, he succeeds who purifies himself﴾ He said: "Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, renounces the rivals (al-andad), and testifies that I am the Messenger of Allah." ﴿And remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ He said: "These are the five prayers, and guarding them and giving them importance."

Then he said: It is not narrated from Jabir except through this chain.

Similarly Ibn Abbas said: the intended meaning is the five prayers, and Ibn Jarir preferred this view.

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to me, Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Khaldah who said: I entered upon Abu al-Aliyah, and he said to me: "When you go out tomorrow to the Eid, pass by me." He said: So I passed by him, and he said: "Have you eaten anything?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you poured water over yourself?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then tell me, what have you done with your zakat?" I said: "As if you are saying: have you directed it?" He said: "I only wanted you for this." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, he succeeds who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾, and said: The people of Medina do not regard any charity as better than it and than providing water.

I say: Likewise we have been related from the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he used to order people to pay the charity of Fitr, reciting this verse: ﴿Indeed, he succeeds who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾.

Abu al-Ahwas said: If one of you is approached by a beggar while he intends to pray, let him put his zakat before his prayer, for Allah says: ﴿Indeed, he succeeds who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: ﴿He succeeds who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ — he purified his wealth and pleased his Creator.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, you prefer the worldly life﴾, meaning: you give it precedence over the matter of the Hereafter, and you place it before what benefits them and their welfare in their livelihood and their return, ﴿while the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾, meaning: the reward of Allah in the Hereafter is better than and more lasting than this world. Indeed the world is lowly and perishing, while the Hereafter is noble and everlasting. So how can a sensible person prefer what perishes over what endures, and concern himself with what will soon leave him, while neglecting concern for the abode of permanence and eternity?!

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Dhuwayd narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Urwah, from Aishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The world is the home of one who has no home, and the wealth of one who has no wealth, and for it gathers one who has no intellect."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Ata, from Arfajah al-Thaqafi who said: I asked Ibn Masud to recite for me: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, and when he reached: ﴿Rather, you prefer the worldly life﴾, he stopped reciting, turned to his companions and said: "We have preferred the world over the Hereafter." The people fell silent, and he said: "We preferred the world because we saw its adornment, its women, its food and its drink, and the Hereafter was hidden from us, so we chose this immediate thing and left the deferred."

This is from him as an expression of humility and self-abasement, or it is a report about the species as such, and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Amr ibn Abi Amr informed me, from al-Muttalib ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever loves his worldly life harms his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter harms his worldly life. So prefer what remains over what perishes." Ahmad alone narrated it.

He also narrated it from Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i, from al-Darawardi, from Amr ibn Abi Amr, with the same wording.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas who said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "All of this—or: this—was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses."

Then he said: We do not know of a report narrated by trustworthy narrators from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas other than this, and another hadith he mentioned before this.

Al-Nasai said: Zakariya ibn Yahya informed us, Nasr ibn Ali informed us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas who said: When ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ was revealed, he said: "All of it is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses." Then when ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled﴾ [an-Najm: 37] was revealed, he said: "He fulfilled." ﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [an-Najm: 38].

That is, this verse is like His saying in Surah an-Najm: ﴿Has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham who fulfilled: that no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and that man will have only what he strives for, and that his effort will be seen, then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense, and that to your Lord is the finality﴾ [an-Najm: 36–42], and the verses to their end. Likewise Ikrimah said, as related by Ibn Jarir from Ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾: it means the verses that are in "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."

Abu al-Aliyah said: The story of this surah is in the former scriptures.

Ibn Jarir preferred that what is meant by His saying ﴿Indeed, this﴾ is a reference to His saying: ﴿He succeeds who purifies himself and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e., the content of this speech, ﴿is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾.

This is a good and strong choice. It has also been related from Qatadah and Ibn Zayd something similar. And Allah knows best.

End of the tafsir of Surah "Sabbih", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
